title: Overlay input isolation and wheel ownership
goal: Make floating windows, toolbox content, dialogs, popovers, and support overlays fully own their pointer, wheel, focus, and context-menu interactions.
must_preserve: Context menu on actual nodes and canvas background
Selection, pan, and zoom when interacting with the scene itself
implementation: Expand overlay target detection to include floating windows, toolbar-safe overlays, dialogs, preview modals, and any overlay root carrying a dedicated data attribute.
Add wheel ownership guards so overlay scroll regions scroll themselves and only the scene host zooms the canvas.
Ensure overlay pointerdown/doubleclick/contextmenu paths do not leak to the scene host.
Use tests and browser automation to prove toolbox group expansion and internal scroll are reliable.
acceptance: Wheel inside toolbox no longer changes scene zoom.
Clicking a toolbox accordion header never starts canvas selection or pan.
Right-click inside toolbox/floating-window content never opens the scene context menu.
Existing node/canvas context menu behavior still works on the scene.

title: Commit-only floating-window persistence
goal: Keep floating-window drag/resize local in JS and persist geometry only on commit or idle.
implementation: Differentiate live geometry updates from committed geometry updates in the JS bridge.
Publish only final geometry after pointerup, minimize, restore, normalize, or hide.
Avoid `PersistCanvasUiStateAsync` on every geometry pulse.
Optionally keep a lightweight local geometry sync for the Blazor markup without server persistence until commit.
acceptance: Zero `SaveViewStateAsync` calls while actively dragging or resizing a floating window.
Exactly one persisted state update after drag/resize commit.
PromptFactory floating toolbox still drags and restores correctly.

title: Commit-only canvas state persistence and UI-state ownership cleanup
goal: Keep pan/zoom/live viewport state in JS during interaction and persist only the final idle/commit snapshot.
must_preserve: Restored view state on page reopen
Selection synchronization for the selection window
Keyboard shortcuts and toolbar zoom controls
implementation: Split high-frequency live state from persisted snapshot state.
Ensure `OnStateChanged` does not trigger DB writes during active pan/zoom/drag.
For ProjectStructure, define domain node X/Y as the persisted source of truth and treat UI `ManualPositions` as transient/local-only for drag in progress.
Keep selected IDs mirrored only as often as the overlay UI actually needs them.
acceptance: No `SaveViewStateAsync` during active pan/zoom.
No `RefreshCanvasSurface()` triggered by pure viewport movement.
ProjectStructure drag no longer persists both domain X/Y and long-lived UI manual positions.

title: Batch node-move persistence
goal: Persist multi-node drag as a single mutation and a single save transaction.
implementation: Introduce a batched move service method that accepts all moved positions in one request.
Perform one `SaveChangesAsync` call for the move batch.
Return enough information for the page to patch local state or reload only once if required.
Make border adoption run after the move commit without turning the move path back into N operations.
acceptance: Multi-node drag produces one service call and one DB save transaction.
Drag commit keeps selected nodes selected.
Moved-node border adoption still behaves correctly.

title: Avoid full surface reloads after simple mutations
goal: Stop calling the heavyweight structure reload path for every non-structural change.
implementation: Introduce a distinction between view-only updates, node-property updates, and structural graph updates.
Patch local surface state for simple node-property changes instead of calling `ReloadSurfaceAsync()`.
Reserve `GetStructureAsync()+SyncGraphAsync()` for true structural invalidation, hierarchy changes, or cases that genuinely require system-managed node recomputation.
Optionally add service methods that return updated node DTOs for local patching.
acceptance: Status/progress/marker/priority changes no longer force full structure reloads.
Inline note edit no longer needs a full reload when only the note node changed.
Create/delete/link flows still end in consistent graph state.

title: Runtime surface cleanup and support/demo separation
goal: Slim the runtime page and clearly separate production authoring UI from support/demo cards.
must_preserve: Outline access if product still wants it
Graph health visibility if product still wants it
implementation: Move CanvasBoundaryCard demo sections behind a debug/sandbox flag or remove them from runtime.
Decide whether Outline and Graph Health belong in runtime, in a collapsible support area, or in diagnostics-only mode.
Keep runtime markup focused on authoring, overlays, and essential support surfaces.
acceptance: ProjectStructure runtime page no longer renders always-on demo cards.
User-facing runtime behavior is clearer and lighter.
Any moved support functionality remains reachable where intended.

title: Instrumentation and browser gates foundation
goal: Add the measurement and screenshot infrastructure required for safe refactoring.
implementation: Add or expand debug counters on `host.__canvasWorkbenchState` for render count, full rebuild count, patched count, and state publish count.
Add browser assertions and screenshots for toolbox behavior, window drag, single-select, multi-select, and key modal flows.
Create a large deterministic graph fixture for browser and local performance validation.
acceptance: Codex can prove improvements with counters and screenshots rather than only with anecdotes.
A failing browser gate is considered a failed task.

title: Retained DOM/SVG renderer for nodes, links, and frames
goal: Keep the current renderer model but make it retained and patch-based rather than rebuild-based.
must_preserve: Node visuals, chips, badges, inline media, annotations
implementation: Introduce keyed maps for node/link/frame elements and patch only what changed.
Keep hot-path pan transform-only wherever possible.
Separate overlay-only rebuilds from scene object patching.
Preserve exported image capture by rendering from the retained DOM/SVG scene.
acceptance: Normal drag/pan no longer clears and rebuilds node and link layers.
Retained element maps stay consistent after create/delete/link/collapse operations.

title: Viewport culling and filtered scene projection
goal: Render only what matters for the current viewport and interaction context.
must_preserve: Links for visible and near-visible nodes
implementation: Compute viewport bounds and only mount/update visible nodes plus a small overscan margin.
Filter links and frames based on visible endpoint membership or viewport intersection.
Keep selection and keyboard behavior correct even when not every node is mounted.
acceptance: Rendered visible node count is materially smaller than total node count on large graphs.
Selection/focus still works when selected nodes move into or out of view.

title: Dirty-region drag loop owned by JS
goal: Keep drag, pan, guides, and affected links entirely in JS with minimal patch scope.
implementation: Track dirty node IDs, dirty link IDs, and dirty guide overlays during drag.
Patch only the changed scene objects during active interaction.
Defer expensive recalculation until drop/commit where possible.
acceptance: Active drag updates only moved nodes, affected links, and active guides.
Guide rendering stays correct while render cost drops materially.

title: Selection-panel decomposition and lazy expensive support surfaces
goal: Reduce the Razor render tree and compute heavy overlay sections only when needed.
must_preserve: Selection window single-select and multi-select behavior
All modal dialogs and advanced details
Runtime launch, transcript, preview, and mermaid actions
implementation: Extract single-select and multi-select panels into focused components or render fragments with stable parameters.
Lazy-render expensive detail sections and support panels only when visible.
Keep the selection window as HTML/Blazor, but minimize page-level recomputation.
acceptance: Selection UI remains feature-complete.
Unrelated viewport changes do not force large overlay recomputation.

title: Scene patch protocol and plain-JS modularization
goal: Make the JS layer maintainable without TypeScript or a new bundler requirement.
must_preserve: Current JS entry points used by tests and Blazor
implementation: Keep plain JavaScript only.
Refactor the giant interop file into clearly owned internal modules or adjacent JS files with a stable public API.
Separate state store, overlay guards, renderer, viewport math, scene patching, diagnostics, and command API.
Do not introduce TypeScript or a heavy build chain.
acceptance: Public API stays stable or is migrated with tests in the same task.
Hot-path JS is easier to reason about and code ownership is explicit.

title: Dedicated screenshot and performance regression suite
goal: Turn the validated runtime states into a maintainable browser regression suite.
must_preserve: Artifact capture used by the team today
implementation: Split ProjectStructure browser coverage into targeted regression tests instead of one oversized smoke file where appropriate.
Capture deterministic screenshots and debug counters for key flows.
Add a large-graph fixture path and performance-oriented assertions.
acceptance: Browser regressions are easier to localize.
Codex can rerun a precise subset of Playwright tests after each subbundle.

title: Optional true-canvas renderer spike
goal: Benchmark an actual canvas renderer only after the current architecture is stabilized and measured.
implementation: Build an isolated benchmark scene and a narrow prototype for nodes, links, and hit testing.
Compare retained DOM/SVG vs true canvas on the same graph tiers.
Document trade-offs: accessibility, text measurement, export path, and overlay integration.
acceptance: A go/no-go decision is backed by measured evidence, not intuition.

title: Optional shared-library consolidation
goal: Retire or intentionally isolate the duplicated canvas component trees after the main fixes are complete.
implementation: Inventory actual consumers, remove dead duplication, and keep one canonical canvas stack.
Do not attempt this early in the program.
acceptance: There is one clearly canonical shared canvas implementation path or an explicitly documented reason for temporary duality.
